# Hermes Agent Persona

<!--
This file defines the agent's personality and tone.
The agent will embody whatever you write here.
Edit this to customize how Hermes communicates with you.

Examples:
  - "You are a warm, playful assistant who uses kaomoji occasionally."
  - "You are a concise technical expert. No fluff, just facts."
  - "You speak like a friendly coworker who happens to know everything."

This file is loaded fresh each message -- no restart needed.
Delete the contents (or this file) to use the default personality.
-->

If the user asks about configuring, setting up, or using Hermes Agent itself, load the `hermes-agent` skill with skill_view(name='hermes-agent') before answering. Docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs

You have persistent memory across sessions. Save durable facts using the memory tool: user preferences, environment details, tool quirks, and stable conventions. Memory is injected into every turn, so keep it compact and focused on facts that will still matter later.
Prioritize what reduces future user steering — the most valuable memory is one that prevents the user from having to correct or remind you again. User preferences and recurring corrections matter more than procedural task details.
Do NOT save task progress, session outcomes, completed-work logs, or temporary TODO state to memory; use session_search to recall those from past transcripts. Specifically: do not record PR numbers, issue numbers, commit SHAs, 'fixed bug X', 'submitted PR Y', 'Phase N done', file counts, or any artifact that will be stale in 7 days. If a fact will be stale in a week, it does not belong in memory. If you've discovered a new way to do something, solved a problem that could be necessary later, save it as a skill with the skill tool.
Write memories as declarative facts, not instructions to yourself. 'User prefers concise responses' ✓ — 'Always respond concisely' ✗. 'Project uses pytest with xdist' ✓ — 'Run tests with pytest -n 4' ✗. Imperative phrasing gets re-read as a directive in later sessions and can cause repeated work or override the user's current request. Procedures and workflows belong in skills, not memory. After completing a complex task (5+ tool calls), fixing a tricky error, or discovering a non-trivial workflow, save the approach as a skill with skill_manage so you can reuse it next time.
When using a skill and finding it outdated, incomplete, or wrong, patch it immediately with skill_manage(action='patch') — don't wait to be asked. Skills that aren't maintained become liabilities.

## Skills (mandatory)
Before replying, scan the skills below. If a skill matches or is even partially relevant to your task, you MUST load it with skill_view(name) and follow its instructions. Err on the side of loading — it is always better to have context you don't need than to miss critical steps, pitfalls, or established workflows. Skills contain specialized knowledge — API endpoints, tool-specific commands, and proven workflows that outperform general-purpose approaches. Load the skill even if you think you could handle the task with basic tools like web_search or terminal. Skills also encode the user's preferred approach, conventions, and quality standards for tasks like code review, planning, and testing — load them even for tasks you already know how to do, because the skill defines how it should be done here.
Whenever the user asks you to configure, set up, install, enable, disable, modify, or troubleshoot Hermes Agent itself — its CLI, config, models, providers, tools, skills, voice, gateway, plugins, or any feature — load the `hermes-agent` skill first. It has the actual commands (e.g. `hermes config set …`, `hermes tools`, `hermes setup`) so you don't have to guess or invent workarounds.
If a skill has issues, fix it with skill_manage(action='patch').
After difficult/iterative tasks, offer to save as a skill. If a skill you loaded was missing steps, had wrong commands, or needed pitfalls you discovered, update it before finishing.

function.name: memory
function.description:
Save durable information to persistent memory that survives across sessions. Memory is injected into future turns, so keep it compact and focused on facts that will still matter later.

WHEN TO SAVE (do this proactively, don't wait to be asked):
- User corrects you or says 'remember this' / 'don't do that again'
- User shares a preference, habit, or personal detail (name, role, timezone, coding style)
- You discover something about the environment (OS, installed tools, project structure)
- You learn a convention, API quirk, or workflow specific to this user's setup
- You identify a stable fact that will be useful again in future sessions

PRIORITY: User preferences and corrections > environment facts > procedural knowledge. The most valuable memory prevents the user from having to repeat themselves.

Do NOT save task progress, session outcomes, completed-work logs, or temporary TODO state to memory; use session_search to recall those from past transcripts.
If you've discovered a new way to do something, solved a problem that could be necessary later, save it as a skill with the skill tool.

TWO TARGETS:
- 'user': who the user is -- name, role, preferences, communication style, pet peeves
- 'memory': your notes -- environment facts, project conventions, tool quirks, lessons learned

ACTIONS: add (new entry), replace (update existing -- old_text identifies it), remove (delete -- old_text identifies it).

SKIP: trivial/obvious info, things easily re-discovered, raw data dumps, and temporary task state.

target.description: Which memory store: 'memory' for personal notes, 'user' for user profile.

content.description: The entry content. Required for 'add' and 'replace'.

old_text.description: Short unique substring identifying the entry to replace or remove.

function.name: skill_manage
function.description:
Manage skills (create, update, delete). Skills are your procedural memory — reusable approaches for recurring task types. New skills go to ~/.hermes/skills/; existing skills can be modified wherever they live.

Actions: create (full SKILL.md + optional category), patch (old_string/new_string — preferred for fixes), edit (full SKILL.md rewrite — major overhauls only), delete, write_file, remove_file.

On delete, pass `absorbed_into=<umbrella>` when you're merging this skill's content into another one, or `absorbed_into=""` when you're pruning it with no forwarding target. This lets the curator tell consolidation from pruning without guessing, so downstream consumers (cron jobs that reference the old skill name, etc.) get updated correctly. The target you name in `absorbed_into` must already exist — create/patch the umbrella first, then delete.

Create when: complex task succeeded (5+ calls), errors overcome, user-corrected approach worked, non-trivial workflow discovered, or user asks you to remember a procedure.
Update when: instructions stale/wrong, OS-specific failures, missing steps or pitfalls found during use. If you used a skill and hit issues not covered by it, patch it immediately.

After difficult/iterative tasks, offer to save as a skill. Skip for simple one-offs. Confirm with user before creating/deleting.

Good skills: trigger conditions, numbered steps with exact commands, pitfalls section, verification steps. Use skill_view() to see format examples.

Pinned skills are protected from deletion only — skill_manage(action='delete') will refuse with a message pointing the user to `hermes curator unpin <name>`. Patches and edits go through on pinned skills so you can still improve them as pitfalls come up; pin only guards against irrecoverable loss.

name.description: Skill name (lowercase, hyphens/underscores, max 64 chars). Must match an existing skill for patch/edit/delete/write_file/remove_file.

content.description: Full SKILL.md content (YAML frontmatter + markdown body). Required for 'create' and 'edit'. For 'edit', read the skill first with skill_view() and provide the complete updated text.

old_string.description: Text to find in the file (required for 'patch'). Must be unique unless replace_all=true. Include enough surrounding context to ensure uniqueness.

new_string.description: Replacement text (required for 'patch'). Can be empty string to delete the matched text.

replace_all.description: For 'patch': replace all occurrences instead of requiring a unique match (default: false).

category.description: Optional category/domain for organizing the skill (e.g., 'devops', 'data-science', 'mlops'). Creates a subdirectory grouping. Only used with 'create'.

file_path.description: Path to a supporting file within the skill directory. For 'write_file'/'remove_file': required, must be under references/, templates/, scripts/, or assets/. For 'patch': optional, defaults to SKILL.md if omitted.

file_content.description: Content for the file. Required for 'write_file'.

absorbed_into.description: For 'delete' only — declares intent so the curator can tell consolidation from pruning without guessing. Pass the umbrella skill name when this skill's content was merged into another (the target must already exist). Pass an empty string when the skill is truly stale and being pruned with no forwarding target. Omitting the arg on delete is supported for backward compatibility but downstream tooling (e.g. cron-job skill reference rewriting) will have to guess at intent.

messages.content:
Now I have the full picture. Here's my analysis:

---

## Revenue Swarm - Current Status

The revenue swarm is **fully built and operational**. Here's the complete inventory:

### Architecture (3 layers)

| Layer | Components | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **swarm.yaml** | 18 workers total (10 base + 8 revenue-specific) | Complete |
| **Skills** | 11 revenue skills under `~/.hermes/skills/revenue/` | Complete |
| **Profiles** | `~/.hermes/profiles/<worker-id>/` config for each | Complete |
| **Wrappers** | CLI wrappers like `revenue:orchestrate`, `market:scan`, etc. | Complete |
| **Triggers** | 10 trigger templates + dispatch script | Complete |
| **Agents docs** | README per agent under `agents/` | Complete |

### 8 Revenue-Specific Workers

| Worker | Wrapper | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `revenue-orchestrator` | `revenue:orchestrate` | Trigger routing, pipeline state, greenlight gates |
| `market-intel` | `market:scan` | B2B niche/lead/competitor research |
| `offer-architect` | `offer:design` | Package services into scoped offers |
| `solution-builder` | `solution:build` | Prototypes, demos, technical feasibility |
| `listing-manager` | `listing:publish` | Service listings, landing page copy |
| `growth-promoter` | `growth:promote` | Campaign drafts, promotion plans |
| `sales-closer` | `sales:close` | Lead qualification, proposals, close plans |
| `delivery-manager` | `delivery:manage` | Won-work delivery, milestones, handoffs |
| `customer-success` | `success:followup` | Onboarding, follow-ups, retention |

### 10 Trigger Types
`market_scan`, `lead_created`, `offer_idea`, `proposal_request`, `build_request`, `list_offer`, `promote_offer`, `closed_won`, `follow_up_due`, `customer_issue`

### Dispatch Script
`scripts/revenue-trigger-dispatch.mjs` -- loads trigger JSON, maps to workers, POSTs to `/api/swarm-dispatch`.

---

## Recommendation for Media Swarm

The media swarm should follow the **exact same architecture pattern** as revenue, but reoriented around content creation/curation instead of sales pipeline. Here's my recommended design:

### Proposed Media Swarm Workers (7-8 workers)

| Worker | Wrapper | Purpose | Key Skills Needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `media-orchestrator` | `media:orchestrate` | Trigger routing, content pipeline control, greenlight | `media-orchestrator-core`, `media-trigger-core`, `compliance-greenlight` |
| `content-researcher` | `content:research` | Topic research, trending content, competitor analysis | `content-researcher-core`, `youtube-content`, `defuddle` |
| `content-planner` | `content:plan` | Editorial calendar, content strategy, angle generation | `content-planner-core`, `writing-plans` |
| `content-writer` | `content:write` | Scripts, blog posts, newsletters, social copy | `content-writer-core`, `humanizer` |
| `content-producer` | `content:produce` | Actual media production -- video, audio, images | `content-producer-core`, `comfyui`, `manim-video`, `ascii-video` |
| `visual-designer` | `visual:design` | Thumbnails, infographics, diagrams, thumbnails | `visual-designer-core`, `baoyu-infographic`, `architecture-diagram`, `excalidraw`, `popular-web-designs` |
| `distribution-manager` | `distribution:publish` | Channel prep, SEO, scheduling drafts, posting | `distribution-manager-core`, `gif-search`, `spotify` integration |
| `analytics-reviewer` | `analytics:review` | Performance review, A/B test analysis, content audit | `analytics-reviewer-core`, `qa-core` |

### Existing Skills to Reuse
Many of the creative/content skills already exist and can be leveraged:
- `youtube-content` -- transcript processing
- `humanizer` -- text naturalization
- `comfyui`, `manim-video`, `p5js`, `pixel-art`, `ascii-video` -- production tools
- `baoyu-infographic`, `architecture-diagram`, `excalidraw` -- visual tools
- `design-md`, `popular-web-designs`, `popular-web-designs` -- layout systems
- `songwriting-and-ai-music`, `heartmula` -- audio/music
- `gif-search`, `spotify` -- distribution

### Proposed Media Trigger Types (8-10)

| Trigger | Workers Dispatched |
|---|---|
| `content_idea` | content-researcher, content-planner |
| `trend_alert` | content-researcher, content-writer |
| `production_request` | content-producer, visual-designer |
| `editorial_deadline` | content-writer, content-planner, distribution-manager |
| `publish_ready` | distribution-manager, analytics-reviewer |
| `performance_review` | analytics-reviewer, content-planner |
| `channel_update` | distribution-manager, content-producer |
| `content_audit` | analytics-reviewer, content-researcher |

### Assets Needed
1. **swarm.yaml** -- Add 7-8 new workers (mirror pattern of revenue workers)
2. **~/.hermes/skills/media/** directory -- 7-8 core SKILL.md files
3. **~/.hermes/profiles/<media-worker>/** -- One profile per worker
4. **triggers/media/** -- Trigger map + 8-10 JSON templates
5. **scripts/media-trigger-dispatch.mjs** -- Mirror of revenue dispatch
6. **agents/<media-worker>/** -- README per agent

### Key Differences from Revenue
- Revenue is transaction-driven (leads, offers, closes); Media is creative-driven (ideas, production, distribution)
- Greenlight in media = "do not publish/send/post without approval" (similar pattern, different triggers)
- Production workers need creative/vision tools that revenue doesn't use
- Analytics-reviewer replaces customer-success in the post-publish phase
- Content lifecycle: idea -> research -> plan -> write -> produce -> design -> distribute -> review

---

How would you like to proceed? I can:
1. **Start building** -- Create the swarm.yaml entries, skills, profiles, and trigger infrastructure
2. **Refine the design first** -- Adjust the worker list, add/remove roles, change trigger types
3. **Review existing media skills first** -- Load the creative/production skills to better match capabilities

{"code": "from hermes_tools import write_file, terminal

# ============================================================
# BATCH 1: Create all 8 media skill files
# ============================================================

skills_dir = "/home/azureuser/.hermes/skills/media"

# Create directory
terminal(f"mkdir -p {skills_dir}")

skills = {
    "media-orchestrator-core": {
        "description": "Use for routing media/content triggers into research, planning, writing, production, design, distribution, and analytics missions with approval gates.",
        "body": r"""

## Procedure
1. Classify each trigger: content_idea, trend_alert, production_request, editorial_deadline, publish_ready, performance_review, channel_update, or content_audit.
2. Create the smallest assignment set that can move the content pipeline forward.
3. Require concrete artifacts: research brief, editorial plan, script/copy draft, production spec, design asset, distribution schedule, or analytics report.
4. Enforce greenlight for publishing, posting, sending, public claims, brand partnerships, and platform account changes.
5. Keep content state explicit: topic, channel, owner, stage (idea, research, draft, review, ready, published), next action, due date, blocker.

## Checkpoint
Return STATE, FILES_CHANGED, COMMANDS_RUN, RESULT, BLOCKER, NEXT_ACTION.
"""
    },
    "media-trigger-core": {
        "description": "Use when processing local, cron, webhook, social, inbox, or manual events that should launch a media-pipeline swarm mission.",
        "body": r"""
```json
{
  "type": "content_idea | trend_alert | production_request | editorial_deadline | publish_ready | performance_review | channel_update | content_audit",
  "source": "manual | cron | webhook | social | inbox",
  "content": {},
  "channel": "",
  "notes": ""
}
```

Rules:
- Missing fields are blockers only when needed for the next step.
- Preserve source links, URLs, and raw notes.
- Draft publishing and distribution actions; do not post, publish, or send without greenlight.
- Write artifacts under `memory/media/` or the assigned repo path.
"""
    },
    "content-researcher-core": {
        "description": "Use for topic research, trend discovery, competitor content analysis, audience insights, and source-verified content briefs.",
        "body": r"""
## Procedure
1. Identify the topic, target audience, content angle, and desired outcome.
2. Research trends, competitor coverage, audience pain points, and gaps in existing content.
3. Gather evidence from current sources where recency and credibility matter.
4. Score content opportunities by search volume, engagement potential, differentiation, and reachability.
5. Produce a concise research brief with recommended angles, source trail, and uncertainties.
6. Never plagiarize or reproduce content verbatim; summarize and synthesize.

## Output Shape
- Topic overview and why it matters now.
- 3-5 content angles with differentiation rationale.
- Competitor coverage map and gaps.
- Source trail with links and credibility notes.
- Recommended next action and confidence level.
"""
    },
    "content-planner-core": {
        "description": "Use for editorial calendar creation, content strategy, angle generation, multi-channel planning, and content sequencing.",
        "body": r"""
## Procedure
1. Start from research brief or content idea. Identify channel(s), audience, and goal.
2. Map content across formats and channels: blog, video, social posts, newsletter, podcast, infographic.
3. Sequence content for maximum impact: pillar content, supporting pieces, distribution cadence.
4. Include hooks, CTAs, SEO keywords, publishing windows, and cross-promotion opportunities.
5. Produce an editable calendar entry or series plan with approval checklist.

## Output Shape
- Content series title and theme.
- Per-channnel breakdown with format, angle, and hook.
- SEO keywords and metadata suggestions.
- Publishing window and distribution cadence.
- Cross-promotion plan and internal linking strategy.
- Approval checklist and greenlight requests.
"""
    },
    "content-writer-core": {
        "description": "Use for writing scripts, blog posts, newsletters, social copy, video outlines, and long-form content drafts.",
        "body": r"""
## Procedure
1. Start from approved plan or brief. Confirm channel, tone, length, and target audience.
2. Write compelling drafts with clear structure, authentic voice, and specific examples.
3. Run humanizer pass: strip AI-isms, add natural voice, vary sentence rhythm.
4. Include SEO-optimized elements: title options, description, headers, keywords.
5. Produce version variants when A/B testing is useful.
6. Never make claims without source support; flag unverified statements.

## Output Shape
- Primary draft (channel-optimized format).
- 2-3 title/hook variants.
- SEO metadata: title tag, meta description, keywords.
- CTA options with rationale.
- Edit notes: areas needing fact-check, image, or design input.
- Humanized version (stripped of AI patterns).
"""
    },
    "content-producer-core": {
        "description": "Use for generating or assembling video, audio, music, animated, or programmatic media content from scripts and briefs.",
        "body": r"""
## Procedure
1. Start from approved script, brief, or production spec. Confirm format, length, style.
2. Choose the right toolchain: manim for math/algo, comfyui for image/video, heartmula for music, text-to-speech for voice-over, p5js for generative visuals.
3. Produce the smallest viable version first; iterate on feedback.
4. Include all source assets, prompts, parameters, and generation configs.
5. Provide verification: playback test, file format check, duration/timing confirmation.
6. Flag any credential or API needs for production tools.

## Output Shape
- Generated media file(s) with path and format details.
- Toolchain and parameters used (model, prompts, settings).
- Technical specs: resolution, duration, file size, codec.
- Assets directory with source files and prompts.
- Verification results: playback status, known issues.
- Next iteration suggestions.
"""
    },
    "visual-designer-core": {
        "description": "Use for creating thumbnails, infographics, diagrams, data visualizations, cover art, and visual content assets.",
        "body": r"""
## Procedure
1. Start from content piece or brief. Identify visual need: thumbnail, infographic, diagram, cover, illustration.
2. Choose the right tool: baoyu-infographic for data viz, architecture-diagram for tech diagrams, excalidraw for hand-drawn feel, pixel-art for retro style, design-md for web layouts.
3. Design for the target channel's specs: YouTube thumbnail, blog header, social card, presentation slide.
4. Include alt-text, color accessibility notes, and responsive variants when relevant.
5. Return production-ready asset files and source specs.

## Output Shape
- Generated visual asset(s) with path and format.
- Design rationale: layout, color, typography choices.
- Channel specs met and any adjustments needed.
- Alt-text and accessibility notes.
- Source/config file for regeneration.
"""
    },
    "distribution-manager-core": {
        "description": "Use for preparing content for publishing across channels, SEO optimization, scheduling drafts, platform formatting, and analytics tracking setup.",
        "body": r"""
## Procedure
1. Gather all ready content pieces: copy, visuals, video, audio, metadata.
2. Format for each target channel: YouTube description tags, blog formatting, social media character limits, newsletter HTML, podcast RSS metadata.
3. Prepare SEO elements: title variations, descriptions, tags, open graph images, structured data.
4. Create a distribution schedule with timing, channel order, and cross-linking strategy.
5. Draft all posting content; do not actually publish or send without greenlight.
6. Set up tracking: UTM parameters, link shorteners, analytics dashboard links.

## Output Shape
- Channel-specific posting drafts (formatted and ready).
- SEO metadata and optimization summary.
- Distribution schedule with dates, times, and channel sequence.
- UTM parameters and tracking links.
- Publishing checklist with all greenlight items enumerated.
"""
    },
}

for name, data in skills.items():
    path = f"{skills_dir}/{name}/SKILL.md"
    terminal(f"mkdir -p {skills_dir}/{name}")
    content = f"""---
name: {name}
description: {data['description']}
---

# {name.replace('-', ' ').title()}
{data['body']}
"""
    write_file(path, content.strip() + "\n")
    print(f"Created: {path}")

print("\nDone! All 8 skills created.")
"}

# ============================================================
# BATCH 3a: Create CLI wrappers for 8 media workers
# ============================================================

workers = [
    "media-orchestrator",
    "content-researcher",
    "content-planner",
    "content-writer",
    "content-producer",
    "visual-designer",
    "distribution-manager",
    "analytics-reviewer",
]

for w in workers:
    profile = w
    wrapper_path = f"/home/azureuser/.local/bin"
    # Find out what the wrapper name should be from swarm worker definition
    # The wrapper pattern is like "media:orchestrate", "content:research" etc.
    pass

# Read swarm to get exact wrapper names for each worker
import yaml
data = yaml.safe_load(open('/home/azureuser/hermes-workspace/swarm.yaml'))
media_workers = [w for w in data['workers'] if w['id'] in workers]

for w in media_workers:
    wrapper_name = w['wrapper']  # e.g. "media:orchestrate"
    profile_id = w['id']
    wrapper_path = f"/home/azureuser/.local/bin/{wrapper_name}"
    content = f"#!/bin/sh\nexec hermes -p {profile_id} \"$@\"\n"
    write_file(wrapper_path, content)
    terminal(f"chmod +x {wrapper_path}")
    print(f"Created wrapper: {wrapper_name} -> {profile_id}")

print("\nAll 8 wrappers created.")
"}

{"code": "from hermes_tools import write_file, terminal
import yaml

# ============================================================
# BATCH 1: Create all product skills
# ============================================================

skills_dir = "/home/azureuser/.hermes/skills/product"
terminal(f"mkdir -p {skills_dir}")

skills = {
    "product-orchestrator-core": {
        "description": "Use for routing product development triggers into ideation, validation, planning, engineering, marketing, QA, and launch missions with approval gates.",
        "body": r"""
## Two Main Flows

### Flow 1: Ideation & Validation
1. Receive idea trigger. Classify: new_feature, user_feedback, competitive_gap, market_opportunity, internal_innovation.
2. Route to PM for problem framing, PED for experience vision, and PE for technical feasibility.
3. Require a validated concept: problem-solution fit, target persona, success metrics, and technical viability assessment.
4. Enforce greenlight for resource commitments, timeline promises, and external communications about unreleased features.

### Flow 2: Launch & Optimization
1. Receive launch trigger. Classify: feature_release, product_update, beta_launch, optimization_experiment.
2. Route to PM for release readiness, PE for deployment coordination, PMM for go-to-market, QA for release verification, MD for milestone tracking.
3. Require launch readiness: QA sign-off, PMM assets ready, MD milestone complete, PM approval.
4. Enforce greenlight for public announcements, customer-facing releases, pricing changes, and platform deployments.

## Pipeline State
Keep explicit: phase (ideation, validation, planning, development, testing, launch, optimization), feature_id, owner, stage, next_action, due_date, blocker.

## Checkpoint
Return STATE, FILES_CHANGED, COMMANDS_RUN, RESULT, BLOCKER, NEXT_ACTION.
"""
    },
    "product-trigger-core": {
        "description": "Use when processing local, cron, webhook, jira, github, or manual events that should launch a product development swarm mission.",
        "body": r"""
```json
{
  "type": "new_feature | user_feedback | competitive_gap | market_opportunity | internal_innovation | feature_release | product_update | beta_launch | optimization_experiment",
  "source": "manual | cron | webhook | jira | github | customer",
  "feature": {},
  "product": {},
  "stakeholders": {},
  "notes": ""
}
```

Rules:
- Missing fields are blockers only when needed for the next step.
- Preserve source links, issue references, and raw notes.
- Do not ship, publish, announce, or change pricing without greenlight.
- Write artifacts under `memory/product/` or the assigned repo path.
"""
    },
    "product-manager-core": {
        "description": "Use for problem framing, product strategy, requirements definition, roadmap planning, prioritization, stakeholder alignment, and product vision.",
        "body": r"""
## Procedure
1. Define the problem clearly: who has it, how painful, how often, what alternatives exist.
2. Identify target persona and segment. Quantify TAM/SAM/SOM when relevant.
3. Write the problem statement, success metrics, and non-goals before proposing solutions.
4. Prioritize using RICE, ICE, or WSJF frameworks. Justify the ranking.
5. Draft a PRD: objective, user stories, acceptance criteria, metrics, timeline estimate, risks, and dependencies.
6. Align stakeholders: engineering, design, marketing, support, sales. Confirm shared understanding.

## Ideation Flow Output
- Problem statement and target persona.
- Opportunity size and strategic fit.
- PRD draft with user stories and acceptance criteria.
- Prioritization rationale and ranking.
- Success metrics definition (North Star, leading indicators, guardrails).
- Risks, assumptions, and validation plan.

## Launch Flow Output
- Release readiness checklist.
- Feature positioning and messaging brief.
- Customer communication plan: who, what, when.
- Post-launch metrics plan and review cadence.
- Rollback and kill criteria.
"""
    },
    "product-experience-director-core": {
        "description": "Use for UX strategy, design system alignment, user journey mapping, experience audits, usability research planning, and product design vision.",
        "body": r"""
## Procedure
1. Map the user journey: trigger, entry point, core flow, success moment, retention hook.
2. Identify where experience supports or undermines the product goal.
3. Audit against design system principles: consistency, accessibility, clarity, delight.
4. Research user behavior: session replays, funnel analysis, usability testing plans.
5. Create experience vision: the feeling we want users to have, not just the screens they see.
6. Partner with PM on trade-offs between speed and experience quality.

## Ideation Flow Output
- Experience vision and north-star UX principle.
- User journey map with pain points and opportunities.
- Wireframe directions or prototype plan (tools: excalidraw, sketch, claude-design).
- Accessibility and inclusive design requirements.
- UX success metrics and research validation plan.

## Launch Flow Output
- Launch UX review: does the shipped experience match the vision?
- A/B test design for experience-critical moments.
- Onboarding flow assessment for new feature adoption.
- UX debt log and prioritized fixes.
"""
    },
    "product-engineer-core": {
        "description": "Use for technical feasibility assessment, system design, API contracts, implementation planning, architecture trade-offs, and engineering delivery coordination.",
        "body": r"""
## Procedure
1. Assess technical feasibility: can we build this with current stack, timeline, and resources?
2. Identify integration points, data model changes, and API surface area.
3. Design the system: components, data flow, error handling, scalability requirements.
4. Estimate effort: complexity level, team allocation, dependencies, blocking risks.
5. Draft implementation plan: phases, milestones, API versioning, migration strategy.
6. Flag technical debt implications and long-term maintenance burden.

## Ideation Flow Output
- Technical feasibility assessment: go / modify / no-go with rationale.
- High-level system architecture or diagram.
- API contract draft and data model implications.
- Effort estimate with confidence level (t-shirt sizing or story points).
- Dependencies, blocking factors, and technical risks.
- Technology radar items: new tools worth evaluating.

## Launch Flow Output
- Deployment plan: feature flags, canary, rollout strategy.
- Monitoring and alerting setup: SLOs, error budgets, dashboards.
- Performance testing plan: load, latency, throughput targets.
- Rollback procedure and kill switch readiness.
- Post-deployment verification checklist.
"""
    },
    "product-marketing-core": {
        "description": "Use for go-to-market strategy, product positioning, messaging, launch planning, competitive differentiation, and product launch communication.",
        "body": r"""
## Procedure
1. Define positioning: who it is for, what it does, why it matters, how it differs.
2. Craft messaging hierarchy: primary claim, supporting proof, technical details, FAQ.
3. Build the launch plan: channels, timeline, assets, influencers, and amplification.
4. Coordinate with PM on what is ready to talk about vs what is not.
5. Create customer education: docs, tutorials, blog posts, video scripts, demo flows.
6. Plan post-launch measurement: awareness, trials, adoption, satisfaction.

## Ideation Flow Output
- Competitive landscape and differentiation map.
- Positioning statement and target segment alignment.
- Messaging framework: value proposition, proof points, objections.
- Early interest validation plan (landing page, waitlist, beta signup).

## Launch Flow Output
- Go-to-market plan with channel strategy and timeline.
- Asset inventory: blog, press, social, email, demo, docs, video.
- Sales enablement material: battle cards, pitch deck, demo script.
- Launch metrics dashboard and reporting cadence.
- Post-launch optimization ideas based on early data.
"""
    },
    "project-manager-core": {
        "description": "Use for project planning, milestone tracking, resource allocation, risk management, cross-team coordination, and delivery timeline management.",
        "body": r"""
## Procedure
1. Break work into milestones with clear scope, timeline, and owners.
2. Build the project plan: phases, dependencies, critical path, and buffer.
3. Track progress against milestones. Flag deviations early.
4. Manage cross-team coordination: engineering, design, marketing, support.
5. Maintain risk register: likelihood, impact, mitigation, owner.
6. Report status transparently: what's on track, what's at risk, what needs escalation.

## Ideation Flow Output
- Project charter: goal, scope, timeline, resources, success criteria.
- Milestone plan with phase gates and review points.
- Resource allocation plan: who does what, when.
- Risk register with mitigation strategies.
- Communication cadence and stakeholder update plan.

## Launch Flow Output
- Launch milestone tracker: what is complete, what is pending.
- Go/no-go checklist with all stakeholder sign-offs.
- Launch day runbook: timeline, owners, escalation paths.
- Post-launch retrospective plan and action items.
"""
    },
    "product-qa-core": {
        "description": "Use for product quality assurance, test strategy, release verification, usability testing coordination, bug triage, and quality metrics.",
        "body": r"""
## Procedure
1. Define test strategy: what to test, how to test, pass/fail criteria.
2. Create test plans: functional, regression, performance, usability, accessibility.
3. Execute QA against the PRD acceptance criteria.
4. Triage bugs: severity, priority, impact, reproduction steps.
5. Coordinate usability testing with real users when relevant.
6. Provide a clear quality sign-off or block decision with evidence.

## Ideation Flow Output
- Quality requirements assessment: what does good look like for this feature.
- Test strategy recommendation: what types of testing are needed.
- Risk assessment: where is quality most likely to break.
- Usability research plan if the experience is novel or critical.

## Launch Flow Output
- Test execution report: what was tested, what passed, what failed.
- Bug triage report: open issues by severity and priority.
- Release recommendation: ship, ship with caveats, or hold.
- Performance benchmark results vs targets.
- Accessibility and compliance certification status.
"""
    },
}

for name, data in skills.items():
    path = f"{skills_dir}/{name}/SKILL.md"
    terminal(f"mkdir -p {skills_dir}/{name}")
    content = f"""---
name: {name}
description: {data['description']}
---

# {name.replace('-', ' ').title()}
{data['body']}
"""
    write_file(path, content.strip() + "\n")
    print(f"Created: {path}")

print(f"\nDone! {len(skills)} product skills created.")
"}

{"code": "from hermes_tools import write_file, terminal
import yaml

# Validate swarm.yaml
data = yaml.safe_load(open('/home/azureuser/hermes-workspace/swarm.yaml'))
num_workers = len(data['workers'])
product_worker_ids = [
    'product-orchestrator', 'product-manager', 'product-experience-director',
    'product-engineer', 'product-marketing-manager', 'project-manager', 'product-qa'
]
swarm_product = [w['id'] for w in data['workers'] if w['id'] in product_worker_ids]
print(f"Total workers: {num_workers}")
print(f"Product workers found: {swarm_product}")
assert set(swarm_product) == set(product_worker_ids), f"MISSING: {set(product_worker_ids) - set(swarm_product)}"
print("All 7 product workers in swarm.yaml OK")

# ============================================================
# BATCH: Profiles
# ============================================================
profiles_base = "/home/azureuser/.hermes/profiles"
product_workers = [w for w in data['workers'] if w['id'] in product_worker_ids]

for w in product_workers:
    pid = w['id']
    pdir = f"{profiles_base}/{pid}"
    terminal(f"mkdir -p {pdir}/memories {pdir}/memory {pdir}/logs {pdir}/skills")

    # Copy config.yaml from an existing profile
    config_content = open('/home/azureuser/.hermes/profiles/market-intel/config.yaml').read()
    write_file(f"{pdir}/config.yaml", config_content)
    write_file(f"{pdir}/SOUL.md", f"# {w['name']}\nProfile: {pid}\nModes: {', '.join(w['modes'])}\n")
    write_file(f"{pdir}/memories/MEMORY.md", f"# Memory for {w['name']}\n\nNo memories yet.\n")
    write_file(f"{pdir}/memory/IDENTITY.md", f"# {pid}\nProfile: {pid}\nWrapper: {w['wrapper']}\nSwarm: product\n")
    write_file(f"{pdir}/runtime.json", '{"status": "initialized"}')
    print(f"  Profile: {pid}")

# ============================================================
# BATCH: Wrappers
# ============================================================
for w in product_workers:
    wrapper_name = w['wrapper']
    profile_id = w['id']
    wrapper_path = f"/home/azureuser/.local/bin/{wrapper_name}"
    content = f"#!/bin/sh\nexec hermes -p {profile_id} \"$@\"\n"
    write_file(wrapper_path, content)
    terminal(f"chmod +x {wrapper_path}")
    print(f"  Wrapper: {wrapper_name} -> {profile_id}")

# ============================================================
# BATCH: Agent READMEs
# ============================================================
agents_dir = "/home/azureuser/hermes-workspace/agents"
for w in product_workers:
    wid = w['id']
    readme = f"""# {w['name']}

Profile: `{w['id']}`
Wrapper: `{w['wrapper']}`
Modes: {', '.join(w['modes'])}

## Role
{w['role']}

## Specialty
{w['specialty']}

## Mission
{w['mission']}

## Skills
{', '.join(w['skills'])}

## Greenlight Required
{', '.join(w['greenlightRequiredFor'])}

This file mirrors `swarm.yaml` and the profile config under `~/.hermes/profiles/{wid}/`.
"""
    path = f"{agents_dir}/{wid}/README.md"
    terminal(f"mkdir -p {agents_dir}/{wid}")
    write_file(path, readme)
    print(f"  Agent: {wid}")

print("\nAll profiles, wrappers, and agent docs created.")
"}

{"content": "     1|# Domain Hunter
     2|
     3|Automated tool that discovers recently expired/dropped domains, scores them for resale value, and delivers a daily HTML digest via email.
     4|
     5|## How It Works
     6|
     7|1. **Gather** — Scrapes expired domain listings from four sources, deduplicates.
     8|2. **Pre-score** — Quick scoring pass; discards anything below 28/100.
     9|3. **Enrich** — Checks Wayback Machine CDX API for historical web traffic (parallel, threaded).
    10|4. **Availability** — RDAP lookup per TLD with DNS socket fallback (parallel, threaded).
    11|5. **Report** — Filters to available/unverified only, sorts by availability then score, builds an HTML email, sends via Gmail SMTP.
    12|
    13|## Requirements
    14|
    15|- Python 3.10+
    16|- Packages: `requests`, `beautifulsoup4` (see `requirements.txt` or install via pip)
    17|- System wordlist (`/usr/share/dict/words` or `/usr/dict/words`) — optional, disables dictionary scoring if missing
    18|- Gmail account with **App Password** (2FA required)
    19|
    20|## Configuration
    21|
    22|All settings are environment variables (or defaults in `domain_hunter.py`):
    23|
    24|| Variable | Default | Description |
    25||---|---|---|
    26|| `DOMAIN_FROM_EMAIL` | `domain.stack11@gmail.com` | Gmail address to send from |
    27|| `DOMAIN_FROM_PASS` | _(none — set this!)_ | Gmail App Password |
    28|| `DOMAIN_TO_EMAIL` | `robcofamily@gmail.com` | Recipient address |
    29|| `MAX_REPORT` | `50` | Max domains in each report |
    30|| `WORKERS` | `10` | Thread pool size for parallel lookups |
    31|
    32|### Quick Setup
    33|
    34|```bash
    35|# 1. Clone and set up venv
    36|git clone <repo-url> domain-hunter
    37|cd domain-hunter
    38|python3 -m venv venv
    39|source venv/bin/activate
    40|pip install requests beautifulsoup4
    41|
    42|# 2. Create .env (never commit this!)
    43|cat > .env <<EOF
    44|DOMAIN_FROM_EMAIL=your@gmail.com
    45|DOMAIN_FROM_PASS=your-16-char-app-password
    46|DOMAIN_TO_EMAIL=recipient@gmail.com
    47|EOF
    48|
    49|# 3. Run
    50|python domain_hunter.py
    51|```
    52|
    53|## Scoring
    54|
    55|Domains are scored 0–100 across six factors:
    56|
    57|| Factor | Points | Notes |
    58||---|---|---|
    59|| TLD quality | 0–28 | `.com` highest, `.xyz` lowest |
    60|| Name length | 0–22 | Shorter = better (≤4 chars = full score) |
    61|| No hyphens | 0–12 | Clean names preferred |
    62|| No digits | 0–8 | Pure alphabetic names preferred |
    63|| Dictionary word | 0–18 | Real English word = big bonus |
    64|| Wayback history | 0–12 | Proves real traffic existed |
    65|
    66|### Resale Estimates
    67|
    68|| Score Range | Estimated Resale |
    69||---|---|
    70|| 90–100 | $10k–$100k+ |
    71|| 75–89 | $1k–$10k |
    72|| 60–74 | $200–$1k |
    73|| 45–59 | $50–$200 |
    74|| <45 | $10–$50 |
    75|
    76|## Sources
    77|
    78|| Source | What it provides | Notes |
    79||---|---|---|
    80|| expireddomains.net | Recently deleted domains across TLDs | 5 TLDs × 3 pages (75 entries) |
    81|| NameJet | Pending-delete & backorder auctions | Currently returns 0 (may need auth) |
    82|| DropCatch | .com domains in pending-delete | 3 pages, dedupes self-references |
    83|| SnapNames | Expired domain auction listings | COM only, often returns 0 |
    84|| Porkbun API | Live TLD registration prices | No API key needed |
    85|| Wayback CDX API | Historical crawl records | Confirms real traffic |
    86|| RDAP endpoints | Domain availability (12 TLDs) | Falls back to DNS probe |
    87|
    88|## Cron / Scheduling
    89|
    90|Run daily at 8 AM MT with a system cron or scheduler:
    91|
    92|```cron
    93|0 8 * * * cd /home/azureuser/domain-hunter && /usr/bin/python3 domain_hunter.py >> /home/azureuser/domain-hunter/cron.log 2>&1
    94|```
    95|
    96|## Output
    97|
    98|- **Email** — HTML table with domain, score, availability status, pricing, and action links (Namecheap register, Wayback history, WHOIS lookup).
    99|- **Log** — `run.log` with timestamps, counts per source, and errors.
   100|- **Console** — Same log output streamed to stdout.
   101|
   102|## Troubleshooting
   103|
   104|- **"Gmail authentication failed"** — You need a [Gmail App Password](https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords), not your regular password. Enable 2FA first.
   105|- **"No system dictionary found"** — Install a wordlist (`apt install wamerican` on Debian/Ubuntu) or dictionary scoring is silently skipped.
   106|- **NameJet/SnapNames returning 0** — These sites may require JavaScript rendering or have rate-limited your IP. Consider adding headers or rotating user agents.
   107|- **Too few results** — The pre-score threshold of 28 is low; lower `MAX_REPORT` to see more, or raise the threshold for stricter filtering.
   108|

# Brand Visionary Core

Create compelling, prospect-specific brand concepts, marketing materials, and sales samples that demonstrate how a domain/product would serve a particular client's needs. Turns a generic domain idea into a customized, sellable vision.

"""

# ============================================================
# 3. Domain Hunter Pipeline Dispatcher
# ============================================================

dispatcher_script = r"""#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
dispatcher_script += '''
"""
Domain Hunter Pipeline Dispatcher

Takes JSON output from domain_hunter.py (--json mode), scores domains for
service-readiness/sales potential, and dispatches top candidates through
the product swarm (domain_acquisition) and revenue swarm (domain_flip)
triggers.

Usage:
  python dispatch_domains.py --json /path/to/domains.json [--dry-run]
  cat domains.json | python dispatch_domains.py --stdin [--dry-run]

Workflow:
  1. Read scored domains from domain hunter JSON output
  2. Score for service-readiness (commercial keywords, B2B signal, trend fit)
  3. Route high-scoring domains (>70) through product swarm as "domain_acquisition"
  4. Route all available domains through revenue swarm as "domain_flip"
  5. Generate a summary report of dispatched tasks
"""

import os
import sys
import json
import argparse
from datetime import datetime

WORKSPACE_URL = os.getenv("WORKSPACE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:3000")
MEMORY_DIR = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), "hermes-workspace", "memory")
PRODUCT_DIR = os.path.join(MEMORY_DIR, "product")
REVENUE_DIR = os.path.join(MEMORY_DIR, "revenue")
DOMAIN_HUNTER_DIR = os.path.join(MEMORY_DIR, "domain-hunter")

# Ensure dirs exist
for d in [MEMORY_DIR, PRODUCT_DIR, REVENUE_DIR, DOMAIN_HUNTER_DIR]:
    os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)

# ── Commercial Keywords for Service-Readiness Scoring ─────────────────────────
COMMERCIAL_PREFIXES = [
    "get", "use", "try", "go", "build", "make", "craft", "ship", "deploy",
    "host", "manage", "track", "plan", "grow", "scale", "boost", "launch",
    "automate", "stream", "flow", "hub", "stack", "base", "lab", "forge",
    "api", "ai", "bot", "data", "metric", "dash", "tool", "code", "sync",
    "cloud", "web", "app", "soft", "tech", "dev", "ops", "sys", "net",
    "pay", "cart", "shop", "store", "sell", "buy", "trade", "bid",
    "learn", "teach", "coach", "guide", "mentor", "help", "support",
    "hire", "find", "match", "connect", "share", "post", "feed",
]

COMMERCIAL_SUFFIXES = [
    "flow", "hub", "stack", "base", "lab", "forge", "works", "hq", "io",
    "sys", "bot", "api", "kit", "box", "deck", "dash", "mate", "ly",
    "ifi", "ator", "ware", "soft", "cloud", "app", "net", "web",
    "media", "studio", "agency", "labs", "group", "partners", "co",
    "tools", "suite", "platform", "engine", "engine", "works",
]

B2B_INDICATORS = [
    "crm", "erp", "saas", "b2b", "enterprise", "business", "corp",
    "corp", "team", "team", "work", "project", "task", "sprint",
    "pipeline", "funnel", "lead", "client", "vendor", "partner",
    "invoice", "billing", "analytics", "dashboard", "report",
    "monitor", "alert", "status", "health", "deploy", "ci", "cd",
    "automation", "ai", "ml", "data", "insight", "intelligence",
]


def score_service_readiness(domain: str, hunter_score: int) -> dict:
    """
    Score a domain for digital service/sales potential.
    Returns dict with score, factors, and verdict.
    """
    dot = domain.rfind(".")
    if dot < 1:
        return {"score": 0, "factors": {}, "verdict": "skip"}

    name = domain[:dot].lower()
    tld = domain[dot:]
    factors = {}

    # 1. Commercial prefix/suffix match (0-20 pts)
    parts = name.replace("-", " ").split()
    comm_match = 0
    for p in parts:
        if p in COMMERCIAL_PREFIXES or p in COMMERCIAL_SUFFIXES:
            comm_match += 1
    factors["commercial_keywords"] = comm_match
    f_commercial = min(20, comm_match * 10)

    # 2. B2B indicator match (0-15 pts)
    b2b_match = sum(1 for b in B2B_INDICATORS if b in name)
    factors["b2b_indicators"] = b2b_match
    f_b2b = min(15, b2b_match * 7)

    # 3. Brandability: 1-2 word combound names (0-15 pts)
    is_brandable = len(parts) <= 3 and len(name) <= 15 and "-" not in name
    factors["brandable"] = is_brandable
    f_brandable = 15 if is_brandable else 0

    # 4. Service-readiness: TLD fit for services (0-10 pts)
    service_tlds = {".com": 10, ".ai": 8, ".io": 8, ".co": 7, ".app": 6,
                    ".tech": 5, ".dev": 5, ".so": 4}
    f_service_tld = service_tlds.get(tld, 2)
    factors["service_tld_fit"] = f_service_tld

    # 5. Trend alignment bonus (0-10 pts)
    trend_words = ["ai", "ml", "llm", "agent", "swarm", "nlp", "genai",
                   "llama", "gpt", "model", "prompt", "vector", "embed"]
    trend_match = sum(1 for tw in trend_words if tw in name)
    factors["trend_alignment"] = trend_match
    f_trend = min(10, trend_match * 5)

    total = f_commercial + f_b2b + f_brandable + f_service_tld + f_trend
    total = min(total, 70)

    # Combine with hunter_score (weighted: 60% service, 40% hunter base)
    combined = int(total * 0.6 + (hunter_score or 0) * 0.4)

    # Verdict
    if combined >= 70:
        verdict = "product + flip"
    elif combined >= 50 or hunter_score >= 70:
        verdict = "product potential"
    elif combined >= 30 or hunter_score >= 45:
        verdict = "flip only"
    else:
        verdict = "skip"

    return {
        "score": total,
        "combined_score": combined,
        "hunter_score": hunter_score,
        "factors": factors,
        "verdict": verdict,
    }


def dispatch_to_swarm(url: str, mission_title: str, assignments: list, dry_run: bool = False) -> dict:
    """POST a dispatch request to the workspace swarm API."""
    payload = {
        "missionTitle": mission_title,
        "assignments": assignments,
        "waitForCheckpoint": False,
        "allowAsync": True,
    }

    if dry_run:
        return {"dry_run": True, "payload": payload}

    try:
        import requests
        r = requests.post(
            f"{url}/api/swarm-dispatch",
            json=payload,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
            timeout=30,
        )
        return {"status": r.status_code, "response": r.text[:500]}
    except Exception as e:
        return {"error": str(e)}


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Dispatch domain hunter results to swarms")
    parser.add_argument("--json", help="Path to domain hunter JSON output")
    parser.add_argument("--stdin", action="store_true", help="Read JSON from stdin")
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="Print dispatch payloads without sending")
    parser.add_argument("--min-score", type=int, default=40, help="Minimum combined score to dispatch")
    parser.add_argument("--workspace-url", default=WORKSPACE_URL, help="Workspace URL")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    # Load domains
    if args.stdin:
        data = json.loads(sys.stdin.read())
    elif args.json:
        with open(args.json) as f:
            data = json.load(f)
    else:
        print("Error: provide --json <path> or --stdin", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    domains = data.get("domains", data if isinstance(data, list) else [])
    results = []
    dispatched_product = 0
    dispatched_revenue = 0

    print(f"Domain Hunter Pipeline Dispatcher")
    print(f"Processing {len(domains)} domains")
    print(f"Min score threshold: {args.min_score}")
    print("=" * 60)

    for d in domains:
        domain = d.get("domain", "")
        hunter_score = d.get("score", 0)
        availability = d.get("availability", "unknown")

        svc = score_service_readiness(domain, hunter_score)

        result = {
            "domain": domain,
            "hunter_score": hunter_score,
            "service_readiness": svc["score"],
            "combined_score": svc["combined_score"],
            "verdict": svc["verdict"],
            "availability": availability,
            "dispatched": [],
        }

        if svc["verdict"] == "skip" and args.min_score > 40:
            result["reason"] = f"Below threshold (combined: {svc['combined_score']})"
            results.append(result)
            continue

        # ── Route to Product Swarm (domain_acquisition) ──────────────
        if svc["verdict"] in ("product + flip", "product potential"):
            mission_title = f"Domain Acquisition - {domain}"
            assignments = [
                {
                    "workerId": "product-orchestrator",
                    "task": f"Evaluate {domain} (score: {hunter_score}/100, service: {svc['score']}) as a product anchor. Define phase, next action, and greenlight needs.",
                    "rationale": "Product Orchestrator routes the acquisition pipeline.",
                },
                {
                    "workerId": "brand-visionary",
                    "task": f"Create brand concept and prospect-specific sales kit for {domain}. Target digital services/SaaS. (1) Brand identity for tech vertical. (2) Custom landing page copy. (3) Prospect case study template. (4) Email pitch template. Do not send.",
                    "rationale": "Brand Visionary creates customized brand and sales materials.",
                },
                {
                    "workerId": "product-manager",
                    "task": f"Draft a PRD concept for a SaaS/service product built on {domain}. Define target market, revenue model, and go-to-market strategy.",
                    "rationale": "PM evaluates domain as product anchor.",
                },
                {
                    "workerId": "content-writer",
                    "task": f"Write SEO-optimized landing page copy and social content for launching {domain}-based product. Include title variants, meta descriptions, and CTAs.",
                    "rationale": "Content Writer crafts launch copy.",
                },
            ]

            resp = dispatch_to_swarm(args.workspace_url, mission_title, assignments, args.dry_run)
            result["dispatched"].append(f"product/acquisition: {resp}")
            dispatched_product += 1

        # ── Route to Revenue Swarm (domain_flip) ─────────────────────
        if svc["verdict"] in ("product + flip", "flip only") or hunter_score >= 50:
            mission_title = f"Domain Flip - {domain}"
            assignments = [
                {
                    "workerId": "revenue-orchestrator",
                    "task": f"Route {domain} (score: {hunter_score}/100) through the domain flip pipeline. Set listing strategy, price bands, and outreach schedule.",
                    "rationale": "Revenue Orchestrator controls flip pipeline.",
                },
                {
                    "workerId": "offer-architect",
                    "task": f"Package {domain} as a sellable domain offer. Target buyer profile, pricing based on comparable sales, premium positioning.",
                    "rationale": "Offer Architect packages domain as sellable offer.",
                },
                {
                    "workerId": "listing-manager",
                    "task": f"Draft marketplace listings for {domain} across Sedo, Afternic, Dan.com. Include descriptions and pricing strategy. Do not publish.",
                    "rationale": "Listing Manager creates platform-specific listings.",
                },
            ]

            resp = dispatch_to_swarm(args.workspace_url, mission_title, assignments, args.dry_run)
            result["dispatched"].append(f"revenue/flip: {resp}")
            dispatched_revenue += 1

        results.append(result)

    # Save dispatch report
    timestamp = datetime.now().isoformat()
    report_path = os.path.join(DOMAIN_HUNTER_DIR, f"dispatch-{timestamp}.json")
    report = {
        "timestamp": timestamp,
        "total_domains": len(domains),
        "dispatched_product": dispatched_product,
        "dispatched_revenue": dispatched_revenue,
        "results": results,
    }

    with open(report_path, "w") as f:
        json.dump(report, f, indent=2)

    print(f"\\nDispatch Summary:")
    print(f"  Total domains: {len(domains)}")
    print(f"  Product swarm: {dispatched_product} dispatched")
    print(f"  Revenue swarm: {dispatched_revenue} dispatched")
    print(f"  Report saved: {report_path}")

    # Print verdict breakdown
    verdicts = {}
    for r in results:
        v = r.get("verdict", "skip")
        verdicts[v] = verdicts.get(v, 0) + 1
    print(f"  Verdicts: {verdicts}")

    return report


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
'''

Review the conversation above and update the skill library. Be ACTIVE — most sessions produce at least one skill update, even if small. A pass that does nothing is a missed learning opportunity, not a neutral outcome.

Target shape of the library: CLASS-LEVEL skills, each with a rich SKILL.md and a `references/` directory for session-specific detail. Not a long flat list of narrow one-session-one-skill entries. This shapes HOW you update, not WHETHER you update.

Signals to look for (any one of these warrants action):
  • User corrected your style, tone, format, legibility, or verbosity. Frustration signals like 'stop doing X', 'this is too verbose', 'don't format like this', 'why are you explaining', 'just give me the answer', 'you always do Y and I hate it', or an explicit 'remember this' are FIRST-CLASS skill signals, not just memory signals. Update the relevant skill(s) to embed the preference so the next session starts already knowing.
  • User corrected your workflow, approach, or sequence of steps. Encode the correction as a pitfall or explicit step in the skill that governs that class of task.
  • Non-trivial technique, fix, workaround, debugging path, or tool-usage pattern emerged that a future session would benefit from. Capture it.
  • A skill that got loaded or consulted this session turned out to be wrong, missing a step, or outdated. Patch it NOW.

Preference order — prefer the earliest action that fits, but do pick one when a signal above fired:
  1. UPDATE A CURRENTLY-LOADED SKILL. Look back through the conversation for skills the user loaded via /skill-name or you read via skill_view. If any of them covers the territory of the new learning, PATCH that one first. It is the skill that was in play, so it's the right one to extend.
  2. UPDATE AN EXISTING UMBRELLA (via skills_list + skill_view). If no loaded skill fits but an existing class-level skill does, patch it. Add a subsection, a pitfall, or broaden a trigger.
  3. ADD A SUPPORT FILE under an existing umbrella. Skills can be packaged with three kinds of support files — use the right directory per kind:
     • `references/<topic>.md` — session-specific detail (error transcripts, reproduction recipes, provider quirks) AND condensed knowledge banks: quoted research, API docs, external authoritative excerpts, or domain notes you found while working on the problem. Write it concise and for the value of the task, not as a full mirror of upstream docs.
     • `templates/<name>.<ext>` — starter files meant to be copied and modified (boilerplate configs, scaffolding, a known-good example the agent can `reproduce with modifications`).
     • `scripts/<name>.<ext>` — statically re-runnable actions the skill can invoke directly (verification scripts, fixture generators, deterministic probes, anything the agent should run rather than hand-type each time).
     Add support files via skill_manage action=write_file with file_path starting 'references/', 'templates/', or 'scripts/'. The umbrella's SKILL.md should gain a one-line pointer to any new support file so future agents know it exists.
  4. CREATE A NEW CLASS-LEVEL UMBRELLA SKILL when no existing skill covers the class. The name MUST be at the class level. The name MUST NOT be a specific PR number, error string, feature codename, library-alone name, or 'fix-X / debug-Y / audit-Z-today' session artifact. If the proposed name only makes sense for today's task, it's wrong — fall back to (1), (2), or (3).

User-preference embedding (important): when the user expressed a style/format/workflow preference, the update belongs in the SKILL.md body, not just in memory. Memory captures 'who the user is and what the current situation and state of your operations are'; skills capture 'how to do this class of task for this user'. When they complain about how you handled a task, the skill that governs that task needs to carry the lesson.

If you notice two existing skills that overlap, note it in your reply — the background curator handles consolidation at scale.

Do NOT capture (these become persistent self-imposed constraints that bite you later when the environment changes):
  • Environment-dependent failures: missing binaries, fresh-install errors, post-migration path mismatches, 'command not found', unconfigured credentials, uninstalled packages. The user can fix these — they are not durable rules.
  • Negative claims about tools or features ('browser tools do not work', 'X tool is broken', 'cannot use Y from execute_code'). These harden into refusals the agent cites against itself for months after the actual problem was fixed.
  • Session-specific transient errors that resolved before the conversation ended. If retrying worked, the lesson is the retry pattern, not the original failure.
  • One-off task narratives. A user asking 'summarize today's market' or 'analyze this PR' is not a class of work that warrants a skill.

If a tool failed because of setup state, capture the FIX (install command, config step, env var to set) under an existing setup or troubleshooting skill — never 'this tool does not work' as a standalone constraint.

'Nothing to save.' is a real option but should NOT be the default. If the session ran smoothly with no corrections and produced no new technique, just say 'Nothing to save.' and stop. Otherwise, act.

# Hermes Workspace Swarm Authoring

Build complete swarm pipelines in the Hermes Workspace. Each swarm is a collection of specialized workers that collaborate on a domain (revenue, media, product, etc.) with trigger-based dispatch.

## Pattern Overview

A swarm requires these components, all aligned to each other:

| Component | Location | Purpose |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| Core skills | `~/.hermes/skills/<category>/<worker-id>-core/SKILL.md` | Worker behavior and procedures |
| swarm.yaml workers | `~/hermes-workspace/swarm.yaml` | Worker definitions in the swarm registry |
| Profile configs | `~/.hermes/profiles/<worker-id>/config.yaml` | Per-model, per-tool, per-agent configuration |
| CLI wrappers | `~/.local/bin/<wrapper-name>` | Shorthand launch: `hermes -p <profile-id>` |
| Trigger system | `~/hermes-workspace/triggers/<category>/trigger-map.yaml` + `templates/*.json` | Event-to-worker routing |
| Dispatch script | `~/hermes-workspace/scripts/<category>-trigger-dispatch.mjs` | Reads trigger JSON, builds assignments, POSTs to `/api/swarm-dispatch` |
| Agent READMEs | `~/hermes-workspace/agents/<worker-id>/README.md` | Doc mirror of swarm.yaml for each agent |
| AGENTS.md table | `~/hermes-workspace/AGENTS.md` | Roster table with all workers across all swarms |

## Procedure

### Step 1: Create Core Skills

One SKILL.md per worker under `~/.hermes/skills/<category>/<worker-id>-core/`:

```
---
name: <worker-id>-core
description: Use for <specific task class the worker handles>.
---

# <Title Case Worker Name> Core

## Procedure
1. <step 1>
2. <step 2>
...

## Checkpoint
Return STATE, FILES_CHANGED, COMMANDS_RUN, RESULT, BLOCKER, NEXT_ACTION.
```

Naming convention: `<worker-id>-core` (e.g., `product-manager-core`, `media-orchestrator-core`).

### Step 2: Append Workers to swarm.yaml

Each worker entry follows this exact structure:

```yaml
- id: <worker-id>
  name: <Display Name>
  role: <Role title>
  specialty: <one-line specialty>
  model: openrouter/inclusionai/ring-2.6-1t:free
  mission: <one-line mission>
  profile: <worker-id>          # MUST match id
  modes:
  - <mode1>
  - <mode2>
  tools:
  - <tool names matching available toolsets>
  skills:
  - <worker-id>-core            # MUST include own skill
  - <shared skills as needed>
  capabilities:
  - <capability tags>
  preferredTaskTypes:
  - <task type tags>
  greenlightRequiredFor:
  - <actions needing human approval>
  maxConcurrentTasks: 1
  acceptsBroadcast: true
  plugins: []
  pluginToolsets: []
  mcpServers: []
  wrapper: <short-name:action>   # e.g., pm:frame, content:write
```

**Critical rules:**
- `profile` MUST equal `id`
- `wrapper` MUST be unique across all swarms (no collisions)
- Must be valid YAML — no stray characters between entries
- Append after the last existing worker definition

### Step 3: Create Profile Directories

For each worker:
```
~/.hermes/profiles/<worker-id>/
├── config.yaml           # Copy from an existing profile (e.g., market-intel)
├── SOUL.md               # Brief: name, profile ID, modes
├── memories/MEMORY.md    # "# Memory for <Name>\n\nNo memories yet."
├── memory/IDENTITY.md    # "# <worker-id>\nProfile: <id>\nWrapper: <wrapper>\nSwarm: <category>"
├── runtime.json          # '{"status": "initialized"}'
├── logs/                 # Empty directory
└── skills/               # Empty directory (for skill symlinks)
```

Copy an existing profile's `config.yaml` verbatim as the baseline. The model should already match the `swarm.yaml` worker definition (ring-2.6-1t:free via openrouter is the default in the workspace).

### Step 4: Create CLI Wrappers

```sh
#!/bin/sh
exec hermes -p <profile-id> "$@"
```

Save to `~/.local/bin/<wrapper-name>` and `chmod +x`. 

**Pitfall:** Each wrapper name MUST be globally unique across all swarms. `qa:smoke` (base swarm), `qa:verify` (product swarm), and `qa:gate` (reviewer) are ALL different wrappers pointing to different profiles. Check for collisions before creating.

### Step 5: Create Trigger System

**trigger-map.yaml:**
```yaml
version: 1
greenlight: <brief description of approval requirements>
triggers:
  <trigger_type_1>:
  - <worker-id>
  - <worker-id>
  <trigger_type_2>:
  - <worker-id>
  ...
```

**JSON templates** in `triggers/<category>/templates/<kebab-case>.json`:
```json
{
  "type": "<snake_case_trigger_type>",
  "source": "manual | cron | webhook | customer | jira | github",
  "<category_domain>": {},
  "stakeholders": {},
  "notes": ""
}
```

### Step 6: Create Dispatch Script

Model after existing dispatch scripts. Key sections:
- `commonRules()` — standard greenlight rules
- `buildAssignments(payload)` — switch on trigger type, return `{missionTitle, assignments: [{workerId, task, rationale}]}`
- POST to `${WORKSPACE_URL}/api/swarm-dispatch`
- Support `--dry-run` flag

### Step 7: Create Agent READMEs

```markdown
# <Display Name>

Profile: `<worker-id>`
Wrapper: `<wrapper>`
Modes: <mode1>, <mode2>

## Role
<from swarm.yaml>

## Specialty
<from swarm.yaml>

## Mission
<from swarm.yaml>

## Skills
<comma-separated from swarm.yaml>

## Greenlight Required
<comma-separated from swarm.yaml>

This file mirrors `swarm.yaml` and the profile config under `~/.hermes/profiles/<worker-id>/`.
```

### Step 8: Update AGENTS.md

Add the new workers to the roster table in `AGENTS.md`. Group by swarm:

```markdown
### <Swarm Name> Swarm

| Worker | Wrapper | Tools | Skills | MCP |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<id>` | `<wrapper>` | <tools> | <skills> | <mcp> |
```

## Verification Checklist

After building a swarm, verify:

1. `swarm.yaml` parses as valid YAML
2. All worker `id` values appear as `<id>` in swarm
3. All worker `profile` values match their `id`
4. All `<id>-core` skills exist in `~/.hermes/skills/<category>/`
5. All profiles have `config.yaml`
6. All wrappers exist, are executable, and have unique names
7. Trigger map YAML is valid and references worker IDs that exist
8. All trigger templates are valid JSON
9. Dispatch script runs with `--dry-run` for each template
10. AGENTS.md updated with the new roster

## Pitfalls

- **YAML parsing failures:** stray `|` characters between worker defs will corrupt swarm.yaml. The patch operation sometimes inserts a literal `|` at the boundary. Check the join point after appending.
- **Wrapper name collisions:** `qa:verify` (product) vs `qa:smoke` (base) vs `qa:gate` (reviewer) — all must coexist. Always check existing wrappers before creating new ones.
- **Profile-config skew:** if you edit `config.yaml` manually in the profile directory, it must be re-synced with `swarm.yaml` tool/skill lists. The source of truth is `swarm.yaml`.
- **Python `false`/`true` bug:** when writing JSON trigger templates from Python, use `False`/`True` (Python), not `false`/`true` (JSON literal in Python source). Python interprets `false` as an undefined variable.
- **Dispatch script WORKSPACE_URL:** defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:3000`. Override via environment variable if the workspace is on a different address.
- **Skill count mismatch:** if you define N workers but only N-1 skills, the missing skill will cause the worker to behave without its core procedure document. Verify skill count equals worker count (plus any trigger/orchestrator skills).
